high.title: August KTB Issuance Plan Points to Yield Curve Flattening
high.summary: KB Securities analyst Ahn Jae-kyun forecasts a flattening of the 10-year to 3-year KTB yield curve, citing two key drivers: (1) the possibility of a tightening move at the Bank of Korea's August Monetary Policy Committee (MPC) meeting, and (2) market concerns surrounding supply pressure in the 2–3 year KTB segment from upcoming issuance. The analyst notes that while the August BOK meeting may introduce some hawkish surprise risk, the event itself should help resolve near-term monetary policy uncertainty, potentially anchoring the front end of the curve.

high.title: USD/KRW NDF Surges 19.40 Won Overnight to 1,442.90 Mid
high.summary: The dollar-won one-month NDF closed at 1,442.90 won (mid) in the New York session, representing a sharp 19.40 won appreciation in the dollar versus the previous Seoul spot close of 1,424.00 won. The bid/ask spread was tight at 1,442.70/1,443.10, suggesting active but liquid offshore pricing. This is a significant overnight move that signals strong bearish KRW sentiment heading into the next Seoul open. The magnitude of the move — nearly 1.4% in a single session — is well above typical daily ranges and will likely force domestic importers and corporates to reassess hedging positions. Traders should watch whether the Seoul onshore market gaps higher at the open and whether the BOK or its agents intervene to smooth the move. The NDF level now implies USD/KRW could test the 1,440–1,445 zone intraday, a psychologically and technically important resistance band. Positioning ahead of the BOK MPB minutes release (August 4) and foreign reserves data (August 5) adds further event risk to monitor closely this week.

high.title: Won Weakens to Mid-1,430s on Iran Strike Risk; Post-Intervention Reversal in Play
high.summary: The dollar-won exchange rate climbed to the mid-1,430 won level as the prior session's KRW strength — driven by coordinated South Korea-Japan FX intervention — was fully reversed. The reversal was catalyzed by geopolitical risk, specifically reports that the U.S. and Israel may strike Iran's energy facilities as early as the weekend, prompting a broad risk-off move and safe-haven dollar demand. The yen simultaneously firmed on fears of additional U.S. intervention, creating a complex cross-currency dynamic for Asian FX desks. For KRW traders, this episode highlights the transient nature of intervention-driven strength when geopolitical tail risks dominate sentiment. A strike on Iranian energy infrastructure would be a stagflationary shock for Korea as a major oil importer, adding upward pressure on inflation and the current account deficit, which would compound structural KRW weakness. Watch Brent crude as a leading indicator — any spike above $90/bbl would materially shift the BOK's calculus on rate cuts and FX tolerance. The mid-1,430s now appears to be the near-term floor post-intervention, with the NDF pointing to further upside in USD/KRW.

high.title: South Korean Bond Futures Decline as U.S. Treasuries Weaken; 10-Year Down 23 Ticks
high.summary: South Korean government bond futures fell in overnight trading, tracking weakness in U.S. Treasuries. The 3-year KTB futures closed at 103.18, down 5 ticks, while the 10-year contract fell a more significant 23 ticks — indicating steepening pressure on the Korean yield curve driven by the long end. Notably, foreign investors were net sellers of 3-year futures (122 contracts net sold), while domestic financial investment firms and retail investors provided partial offsetting demand. The 10-year move is particularly significant for portfolio managers holding duration, as it signals that offshore yield repricing is transmitting directly into Korean bond markets. The foreign selling in futures raises concerns about sustained capital outflows from Korean fixed income, which would also add to KRW depreciation pressure through the current account of the financial account. With the BOK MPB minutes due August 4, any hawkish signals — even in the context of the prior July 16 meeting — could amplify yield upside further. Bond investors should reduce duration exposure tactically while monitoring whether foreign net selling accelerates in the coming sessions.

high.title: U.S.-Japan Coordinated Yen Intervention — First Joint Action in Nearly 30 Years
high.summary: The United States and Japan conducted their first coordinated FX intervention in approximately 30 years, jointly acting to support the yen after USD/JPY rose to the mid-160 level during early New York trading on July 31. The dollar-yen quickly reversed following speculation of U.S. Treasury involvement, dropping sharply from the 159 range. This is a landmark development for Asian FX markets broadly. For KRW traders, the implications are twofold: first, coordinated G7 intervention signals heightened tolerance for active FX management across the region, lending legitimacy to and potentially emboldening the BOK's own parallel intervention in the won (as referenced in Article 4). Second, a stronger yen structurally competes with KRW as an Asian export currency, and yen appreciation could reduce pressure on Korean exporters in the near term. However, yen strength also often correlates with risk-off positioning, which is net negative for KRW. The durability of this intervention effect will be key — if USD/JPY re-tests 160, another round of volatility across Asian FX, including KRW, is likely. This development significantly raises the geopolitical and monetary policy complexity for the week ahead.

high.title: US and Israel Reportedly Preparing Strike on Iranian Energy Infrastructure "As Early as This Weekend"
high.summary: Reports from CBS News indicate that the United States and Israel are potentially preparing coordinated military strikes on Iranian energy infrastructure — including power plants and refineries — as early as this weekend. While this is a geopolitical story originating from the Middle East, the market implications for Korean financial assets are direct and significant.

medium.title: Japan's MOF Says It Has Means to Secure Dollars, Including Borrowing Against US Treasuries
medium.summary: Japan's Ministry of Finance publicly signaled — via posts on X in both English and Japanese — its capacity to procure US dollars through cooperation with US authorities, including the ability to borrow against its US Treasury holdings. This appears designed to bolster the credibility of potential yen-buying, dollar-selling FX intervention conducted jointly with the Bank of Japan. While this is a Japan-specific development, it carries indirect relevance for KRW: any large-scale JPY appreciation driven by coordinated intervention could create regional FX spillovers, as JPY and KRW often move in tandem against the USD in risk-off environments. KRW traders should monitor USD/JPY closely as a leading indicator of broader Asian FX direction, and watch for any BOK response if USD strength reasserts itself across the region.

medium.title: Next Week's Schedule for Ministry of Finance and Other Economic Ministries
medium.summary: The upcoming week features several macro data releases relevant to KRW and rates markets. Key highlights include: July 2026 Consumer Price Index (CPI) data due Tuesday, August 4 at 08:00–09:00 KST — a critical input for the BOK's August MPC decision and KRW trajectory. A Price-Related Vice Ministers' Meeting is also scheduled for August 4, signaling government-level attention to inflation dynamics. The Deputy Prime Minister's Cabinet Meeting on Tuesday adds a policy dimension. KRW and KTB traders should treat the July CPI print as the single most important data point of the week — a hot reading would reinforce hawkish BOK expectations and support KRW, while a softer print could ease rate pressure and steepen the curve.

medium.title: South Korean Financial Regulators Weekly Schedule: BOK, FSC, FSS — August 3–7, 2026
medium.summary:
Two high-impact data releases are scheduled this week that are directly relevant to KRW and rates traders. On **August 4 (Tuesday at 16:00)**, the BOK will release the **minutes of the July 16 Monetary Policy Board meeting** — these will be closely scrutinized for the vote breakdown, dissenting views on rate cuts or holds, and any forward guidance language. On **August 5 (Wednesday at 06:00)**, the BOK will publish **end-July foreign exchange reserves**, which will reveal whether reserve drawdowns occurred due to intervention operations and the scale of official FX market activity. Given the confirmed intervention events this week, the reserves data will be a critical post-facto measure of the BOK's firepower deployment. A notable drawdown in reserves would confirm aggressive intervention and may raise questions about sustainability of future defense operations. Fund managers should position ahead of both releases.

medium.title: Conflicting Investor Flows Drive Double the Market Volatility in Korean Equities
medium.summary:
A new research report from the Korea Capital Market Institute identifies four key empirical drivers behind elevated Korean equity market volatility in 2025, with the primary culprit being conflicting trading patterns across different investor types. The study by senior research fellows Kim Jun-seok and Jang Geun-hyuk highlights that domestic retail, institutional, and foreign investor flows are increasingly working at cross-purposes, amplifying intraday and intraweek price swings beyond those seen in comparable major markets. For KRW and bond traders, elevated equity volatility is a relevant indirect signal — heightened KOSPI volatility has historically coincided with increased FX hedging demand, wider KRW bid-ask spreads, and potential foreign equity outflows that pressure the won. It also reflects broader uncertainty in Korean risk assets that international fund managers should factor into position sizing and stop-loss calibration.

---

medium.title: KOSPI Surges 1,000 Points in Single Day, Shattering Multiple Records
medium.summary:
While equity market news falls outside the core brief mandate, this event carries meaningful cross-asset relevance. The KOSPI recording its largest-ever single-session point and percentage gain, combined with foreign investors posting their biggest-ever net buying on record, signals a significant surge in risk appetite toward Korean assets. Such a dramatic foreign inflow event is highly relevant for KRW dynamics — sustained foreign equity buying typically generates substantial USD-to-KRW conversion demand, providing direct upward pressure on the Won. Fund managers should monitor whether this equity-driven capital inflow translates into KRW appreciation momentum in spot FX markets, and whether the BOK may lean against excessive KRW strength via intervention. The sharp retail net selling (record outflow) on the other side of the trade is also notable — it may suggest domestic investors are rotating out of equities into other asset classes, potentially including bonds. Watch for follow-through foreign buying in subsequent sessions and any BOK commentary on FX volatility.
